body:
`make install` puts the console script on `.venv/bin/` and its closing message tells the operator to run it from there — every instance operator then invents the last step themselves (activate the venv, prefix the path, or hand-roll a symlink). The gap bites twice:

- **Gate commands spawn the CLI by bare name.** The shipped T4 row runs `{{ cli_name }} contribcheck` via /bin/sh; on a fresh render + `make install` that fails command-not-found until the operator puts `.venv/bin` on PATH or links the script. The pdca-pdca instance hit exactly this on its first offline cycle.
- **`cli_name` namespacing exists so several instances share one machine** (copier.yml recommends e.g. "pdca-gramps") — i.e. the design already assumes instances coexist on one PATH, but nothing ships that last hop.

Proposal: teach the bootstrap (`scripts/bootstrap-tools.sh`, i.e. `make install`) to symlink `.venv/bin/<cli_name>` into `~/.local/bin/<cli_name>` when that directory exists and is on PATH — idempotent like every other bootstrap step, one `OK|INSTALLED` row, a WARN with the exact `ln -s` command when `~/.local/bin` is absent or off PATH rather than guessing at shell profiles. The namespaced name makes collisions a non-issue by construction; a literal `pdca` cli_name still just works for the single-instance case. `make install-check` reports the row without creating it.

Verified shape on the pdca-pdca instance: a symlink suffices with no activation — the console script's shebang pins the venv interpreter absolutely, and a bare `sh -c '<cli_name> contribcheck'` resolves through it (the T4 gate path).
title: make install: optionally expose the namespaced console script on PATH (~/.local/bin symlink)
